chunks: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said: I heard him say:
Every person is held in pledge on the Day of Judgment by their ʿaqīqah, and the ʿaqīqah is more obligatory than the sacrificial offering (uḍḥiyah).

key_terms.أَوْجَبُ: more obligatory or more strongly required
key_terms.الْأُضْحِيَّةِ: the sacrificial offering of Eid al-Aḍḥā
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: the ʿaqīqah offering for a child
key_terms.بِعَقِيقَتِهِ: by his ʿaqīqah, the sacrificial rite associated with a newborn
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, when people are reckoned

ai.seo_question: How important is the ʿaqīqah in Islam according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith emphasizes the strong importance of the ʿaqīqah for a child, linking it to one's standing on the Day of Judgment. It also states that the ʿaqīqah carries greater obligation than the uḍḥiyah, showing its special legal and familial significance.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4710 - Umar ibn Yazid narrated from Abu Abdullah (as) who said: "
Every person is held in pledge on the Day of Judgment by their Aqiqah, and the Aqiqah is more obligatory than the sacrificial offering (Udhiyyah)."
